recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In this members' only Zoom workshop hosted by Kalina Lux of Templis Aquaria, InnerVerse host and Biofield Tuning practitioner Chance Garton presents a wide ranging introduction to the ether, the human biofield and vibrational sound healing. He walks through his slides on coherent sound, biophotons, psychic vampirism, solfeggio tones and Eileen Day McKusick's biofield anatomy, chakra by chakra, then answers questions. The evening closes with group vowel toning and a full remote tuning fork session with affirmations.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The ether as the medium of healing", "body": "Chance Garton describes the ether as a luminous, plasma like medium out of which all energy and matter emerge, and he equates it with spirit, citing Wilhelm Reich's Ether, God and Devil. In his framework, each person's biofield is a small copy of that universal field, bounded like a cell by a plasma membrane, and he holds that memory lives in this field rather than in the brain. He presents these ideas as an intellectual scaffolding for the practice, openly noting that not every element has been proven in a materialist scientific sense."}, {"title": "Coherent sound and the pull toward harmony", "body": "Chance Garton contrasts coherent sound, such as a well made tuning fork, with the dissonant hum of refrigerators, engines and wireless signals that he believes keeps the body braced and tense. He calls the tendency toward order centropy, and points to metronomes falling into sync as an image of harmony winning out over disharmony. From there he shares his own reading of the number patterns in the solfeggio tones, compares them with the gentler solar harmonic set, and explains why he recommends the Sonic Slider, a weighted fork designed by Eileen Day McKusick, for people starting out."}, {"title": "Leaking light, boundaries and psychic vampirism", "body": "Drawing on research into biophotons, the faint light living cells emit, Chance Garton proposes that stress, injury and trauma cause people to leak light and life force from their field. He links this to Joe H. Slate's book Psychic Vampires and to what he calls the Messiah psyop, the cultural belief that the best people pour their energy out for others. His alternative is to become a lantern: someone who holds their own light with integrity, so that others see themselves more clearly simply by being nearby, and who gives only what flows easily without depletion."}, {"title": "Reading the biofield map, side by side", "body": "Working from Eileen Day McKusick's biofield anatomy hypothesis, Chance Garton walks through the field like the rings of a tree, with birth at the outer edge and the present near the body. He explains her pattern of left side imbalances tied to letting go and the feminine, right side ones tied to moving forward and the masculine, then adds a front and back axis of doing versus thinking. He also shares observations from his own sessions, such as the ankles as an axis of procrastination and perfectionism, along with his coined word procrastinfectionism, illustrated by his early habit of over editing his podcast."}, {"title": "Shared intention and community healing", "body": "Kalina Lux of Templis Aquaria frames the gathering as part of many small communities knitting together, and asks everyone to hold intentions for their collective projects as well as themselves. Chance Garton agrees that group intention amplifies the work, and leads a vowel toning exercise adapted from Sol Luckman before a full group sound healing, pairing each chakra zone with spoken affirmations. Kalina describes Templis Aquaria as a network where members teach members, and argues that inner practice and practical community building each need the other so a community neither gets stuck nor spun off."}]
